title: Asymmetric Judge Error and Clustered Frames: A Pre-Registered Audit of a Commercial Dataset Quality Claim
description: Commercial dataset vendors advertise corpus quality with statistics produced by a vision-language model applied once to a sample of frames. We audit one such claim. Build AI publishes, for its Egocentric-10K corpus, that 96.42% of frames show at least one hand and 91.66% show active manipulation, both ahead of Ego4D and EPIC-KITCHENS-100, from 10,000 frames labelled once with no human label, no interval, and no test that the labeller scores the compared corpora on the same scale. We pre-registered a protocol, replicated the figures with an independent open-weights judge on two releases a year apart, collected 153 human labels from one rater against a written rubric, and re-estimated the published quantities with prediction-powered inference. Three findings. First, judge error is strongly asymmetric: on the hand-visibility indicator the published figure reports, the judge over-calls 6 of the 24 frames where over-calling was possible and under-calls 0 of 129, and on manipulation 10 of 33 against 2 of 120, both significant at p < 10^-5. Second, the corpus is clustered by camera wearer, with a design effect of 1.25 to 1.66 on two independent 10,000-frame draws, so an independent-frames interval understates its width by 11 to 22%; no interval is published, and the released frames carry no identifier that would let anyone else compute one. Third, the comparative claims cannot be resolved at this gold size: correcting both sides of the manipulation margin against EPIC-KITCHENS-100 moves it from a published +6.62 to -1.02 percentage points, 95% interval [-11.68, +9.65], which covers the published value. None of the pre-registered hypotheses was confirmed, and we report what moved when we collected more labels. Artifacts and protocol are public; the measurement card reports NOT_VERIFIED. Not peer reviewed. Code and protocol: https://github.com/caiotheodoro/vernier
